summary.title: SPEC CPU: The Next Generation
summary.one_liner: The arXiv paper describing how the SPEC CPU 2026 benchmark suite was built, including its workload selection, its multithreaded and microarchitecturally diverse benchmarks, and the Rolling-Round-Robin Rate method for multiprogrammed runs.
takeaways: SPEC CPU 2026 is presented as the next-generation SPEC CPU suite for measuring processor performance.
Workloads are drawn from modern open-source applications, chosen and hardened for diversity, portability, and software longevity.
Rolling-Round-Robin Rate is introduced as a standardized way to run heterogeneous, multiprogrammed workloads.
The suite adds more multithreaded benchmarks and workloads with distinct microarchitectural profiles.
The paper focuses on the community-driven methodology for benchmark selection, adaptation, and validation.
summary.summary: This arXiv paper (submitted May 2026, Performance category) describes the methodology behind SPEC CPU 2026, a new generation of SPEC's CPU benchmark suite. It explains a community-collaborative process in which open-source applications were selected and adapted for workload diversity, portability, and longevity. Its main stated contribution is the Rolling-Round-Robin Rate, a standardized method for running heterogeneous, multiprogrammed workloads. The page is an abstract listing only; the full methodology and results are in the PDF/HTML version, which was not reviewed here.
